question:
A 36-year-old woman experienced a severe anaphylactic reaction to amoxicillin and is now presenting
with reduced urine output. Blood tests reveal the following: CBC shows RBC 4500, Hb 13.5 mg/dL,
WBC 8000, and PLT 180,000. Her creatinine level is 1.6 mg/dL. Despite receiving regular fluid
infusions, her urinary output remains low, and her creatinine levels continue to rise. Urinalysis shows
no blood, WBCs, or protein. Which of the following statements is correct? Answer Choices: (A)
Pre-renal azotemia always progresses to ATN if left untreated for more than 48 hours (B)
Contrast-induced nephropathy and sepsis share similar pathophysiological mechanisms in causing
ATN (C) The S3 segment of the proximal tubule is relatively resistant to ischemic injury compared to
other nephron segments (D) In ATN the final change microscopically is changes of the apical brush of
the tubular cells and loosening of the junctions with the membrane (E) Prognosis of acute tubular
necrosis is unrelated to the prognosis of the cause of it and it’s treatment and outcome (F) Damage by
toxic agents is different to those from ischemia (G) The medullary thick ascending limb is most
susceptible to hypoxic injury due to its high metabolic demands (H) Recovery from ATN is dependent
on the regenerative capacity of tubular epithelial cells regardless of the initial insult (I) The least
effected places are the proximal staining tubule and thick ascending limb of loop of Henle- the part in
the medulla (J) Rhabdomyolisis, crystals and multiple myeloma are also risk factors
 A. The least effected places are the proximal staining tubule and thick ascending limb of loop of
Henle- the part in the medulla
B. Prognosis of acute tubular necrosis is unrelated to the prognosis of the cause of it and it’s
treatment and outcome
C. Rhabdomyolisis, crystals and multiple myeloma are also risk factors
D. The medullary thick ascending limb is most susceptible to hypoxic injury due to its high metabolic
demands
E. Damage by toxic agents is different to those from ischemia
F. Recovery from ATN is dependent on the regenerative capacity of tubular epithelial cells
regardless of the initial insult
G. In ATN the final change microscopically is changes of the apical brush of the tubular cells and
loosening of the junctions with the membrane
H. Contrast-induced nephropathy and sepsis share similar pathophysiological mechanisms in
causing ATN
I. The S3 segment of the proximal tubule is relatively resistant to ischemic injury compared to other
nephron segments
J. Pre-renal azotemia always progresses to ATN if left untreated for more than 48 hours
